verdicts.evidence: `i < 0` -> `i <= 0` differs only for a problem that STARTS with the ` — ` separator (brief empty, fix the rest, versus brief the whole string). Measured: of 4,545 direct cases, the 378 that differ are exactly those carrying such a problem (a second battery: 21 of 21 differing verdicts contain one, 0 without). No problem the gate emits has that shape: every producer starts it with a word (`not accounted for…`, `typed pointer…`, `rule removed…`, the seal and corpus texts, UNBOUND_CAUSE_TEXT, `<deliverable> missing`), and the 121 command runs over eleven missions, including every refusal family, are byte-identical. Survived the CI unit pass on this branch and the whole-net pass of 2026-09-29 (scripts/mutation-wholenet.mjs, seven legs, serial). Measurement: identical on all 11 missions × 11 commands (121 runs); 378 of 4545 direct calls differ. Probe suite 2026-09-28 (scratch recipe, reproduced in the PR): eleven missions built with the pristine 0.42.3-dev build — `init` (blank), `init --example`, and the example with a dead pointer, the regulated tier on, a drifted seal, an edited and a removed rule, a failing after-hook, no scaffold-lock (unrecorded corpus), an under-filled framing note, a DRAFT ADR, and a fresh mission with two agent ratifications. Each mutant was spliced alone into dist/lib and eleven commands were run on each mission (check with and without --strict, --json, --sarif, --hooks; gate-hook for claude, cursor and gemini), exit code, stdout and stderr compared byte for byte with the pristine build. Positive control: the killed mutants gate-hook L77 and sarif L161 applied the same way differ on the regulated mission.

verdicts.evidence: `if (fix)` forced true also counts a null instruction under the key null.
